goal: An admin request from a session at aal1 whose account has never verified a second factor makes no call to Supabase Auth, while an account with a verified factor is still held at the challenge on every request.
why: Every page render, server action and poll from a session without two-step makes 1 getUser() call over HTTP to Supabase Auth (2 per save: the action and its redraw); after the step that is 0 for an account with no factor and still 1 for an account whose mirror says it has one.

commits.title: Every account with a verified second factor has it in the mirror: a one-time reconcile and one at each sign-in

changes.how: Make it with 'pnpm exec drizzle-kit generate --custom --name two_step_mirror_reconcile', then run 'node scripts/prune-snapshots.mjs'. Body, data only: 'do $$ begin if to_regclass(''auth.mfa_factors'') is not null then update commerce.accounts a set two_step_since = now() where a.two_step_since is null and a.auth_user_id is not null and exists (select 1 from auth.mfa_factors f where f.user_id = a.auth_user_id and f.status = ''verified''); end if; exception when insufficient_privilege then raise notice two-step mirror reconcile skipped: no read on auth.mfa_factors; end $;' (single quotes as SQL needs them). The guard makes it do nothing where Supabase's auth schema is absent (PGlite in src/db/commerce.test.ts, CI's Postgres service). If the role that applies migrations may not read auth.mfa_factors the block says so and changes nothing; the owner’s count after the deploy (after_deploy) then shows whether any account is left. It only sets a mirror that is null; it never clears one. First line comment: why (the mirror starts to decide when the Auth call may be skipped, so it must be right for accounts that exist today).

In admit(supabase, user) (line 17), after the account is found and before 'return "admitted"': reconcile the mirror from the Auth SERVER's own list. Call 'const { data: fresh, error } = await supabase.auth.getUser()'. If it errors or returns no user: sign the person out (await supabase.auth.signOut()) and return 'no-access' (fail closed: a session must not start with an unknown mirror). Otherwise 'const verified = (fresh.user.factors ?? []).some((f) => f.status === "verified")' and run one statement: when verified, 'update commerce.accounts set two_step_since = coalesce(two_step_since, now()) where id = ${account.id}::uuid'; when not verified, 'update commerce.accounts set two_step_since = null where id = ${account.id}::uuid and two_step_since is not null'. Never read user.factors from the 'user' argument or from getSession(): only getUser()'s answer. Do not touch two_step_reenrol_at.

Add cases for admit() with fakeSupabase(state) from src/server/trust-fixtures.ts (add signOut to the fake if it lacks it, recording 'signOut' in state.calls): (1) the server holds a verified factor and the account's mirror is null: after admit() two_step_since is set; (2) the server holds no factor and the mirror is set: after admit() it is null; (3) state.userError = true: admit() returns 'no-access' and 'signOut' is in state.calls; (4) the cookie's copy (cookieFactors) says verified while the server says none: the mirror stays null.

commits.title: No Supabase Auth call per request for an account that has never verified a second factor

changes.how: In readSession() (lines 120 to 180). Today: 'if (level === "aal1" && !killSwitch) { ...getUser()... }'. Change the condition so getUser() is called only when the mirror or the re-enrol mark says it is needed: 'const mirrorSaysNone = !row.two_step_since && !row.two_step_reenrol_at; if (level === "aal1" && !killSwitch) { if (mirrorSaysNone) enrolled = false; else { ...the existing try/catch with getUser(), unchanged... } }'. So: mirror null and no re-enrol pending: enrolled = false with no call. Mirror set, or re-enrol pending: the call is made exactly as today, and a failure still gives enrolled = null (fail closed). aal2 and the kill switch are unchanged. Then move the two writes below (the mirror update at lines 158 to 163 and the break-glass audit insert at lines 164 to 174) into after() from 'next/server' so they never hold a page: 'after(async () => { try { ...the same statements... } catch {} })'; where after() throws because there is no request scope (a unit or int test calling readSession directly), fall back to running them inline: wrap as the repo's own helper does (src/server/sign-in.ts uses afterAnswer(): use that helper if it does exactly this). Update the comment above the block: the mirror is no longer 'never read for access': it decides only when the Auth call may be skipped for an account that has never verified a factor, it is written when a factor is verified (two-step.ts line 190), cleared on every removal and reset (lines 264, 341, 362), and reconciled at each sign-in (sign-in.ts admit()).

Line 8 of the header comment says 'accounts.two_step_since is a mirror for display and decides nothing'. Replace that sentence with: 'accounts.two_step_since is the app's mirror of a verified factor: it is shown on the Team page, and it decides one thing only: an aal1 session of an account whose mirror is empty skips the getUser() call. It is written when a factor is verified, cleared when one is removed or reset, and reconciled from getUser() at every sign-in.' No code changes in this file.

The header comment (about line 32) says the same 'mirror for display': correct it with the same sentence. Then check the order of writes at line 190 (enrolment verified): the mirror must be set in the same action that verifies the factor, right after the Auth server's verify succeeds, and a failure of that update must fail the action (do not swallow it): if the update is inside a try/catch that ignores errors, take it out of that catch. Change nothing else.

Add a describe 'the Auth call per request' using fakeSupabase(state) and state.calls. Each case runs the gate's read twice (two requests: call the uncached function the test file already uses to read a session; if it only reaches the React-cached readSession, add and export an uncached 'readSessionNow' in auth.ts that readSession wraps, and call that). Cases: (a) aal1, no factor, mirror null: state.calls holds 0 'getUser' after two runs and the account is let in (assurance enrolled false); (b) aal1, the server holds a verified factor, mirror set: 1 'getUser' per run and the session is held at the challenge (getAccount() is null and the gate says challenge); (c) enrol: run the enrol and verify flow of two-step.ts with the fake, then a NEW aal1 session of that account: held at the challenge (the mirror was set by the flow); (d) remove (the account's own switch-off, two-step.ts line 341): afterwards an aal1 session makes 0 getUser calls and is let in; (e) reset by an owner or platform admin (line 362): two_step_reenrol_at is set, so an aal1 session makes the getUser call and is held at enrolment; (f) re-enrol after the reset: mirror set again, an aal1 session is held at the challenge; (g) aal1, mirror set but getUser fails (userError): held (enrolled null), as today; (h) the cookie's copy claims no factors while the mirror is set: still held; (i) kill switch on: 0 calls, as today.

migration.notes: One custom migration (drizzle-kit generate --custom, then node scripts/prune-snapshots.mjs): a guarded data update of commerce.accounts.two_step_since from auth.mfa_factors, no schema change. commerce.accounts is not on the hot-table list, the update touches only rows with a verified factor and a null mirror (a handful), and it adds nothing the running code reads differently: the code deployed before it treats the column as display only. CI's release job applies it before the deploy; never apply it by hand. It must be in the first commit, so the mirror is right before the second commit starts to trust it; push the second commit only after the first has deployed.
